A grain overlay across the whole screen, like old film stock. It does not change the catalog or your progress — visual only. Off by default.

Rank describes where you are on your cinephile path. There are 10 ranks, from Novice to Master, and it never goes backwards.

It is calculated from what you have actually watched: the volume of films, the diversity of territories (countries, eras, currents, authors) and how deeply you have explored them. A more demanding or rarer film weighs a little more than a very accessible one, without ever dominating the score.

Badges and quests enrich this path, but rank remains a global reading of your exploration. Level and XP mostly measure consistency — that is not the same thing as rank.
This clears watched films, badges, completed collections, XP, rank and quests. The editorial catalog stays in place. This cannot be undone.
In 16th-century Japan, villagers hire seven samurai to protect their harvest. A work about solidarity, courage and the price of victory.

Pick up to 3 unlocked badges. They appear centered on your Profile.
You already follow %1$d collections. Finish one, or unfollow one you are not watching, before adding another.
Follow the Initiation collection and mark a film as watched to unlock the rest of First Screenings.
To open “%1$s”, follow at least %2$d collection(s) in “%3$s” and mark at least %4$d films in each.

A collection is an editorial path of related films (a current, a country, an author…). You can follow up to 10 at a time. They appear on Home as long as they are not 100 % complete or still locked. Start with Initiation: follow it and mark at least one film as watched to unlock the rest of the catalog. Harder groups (Film club, Darkened theater…) stay locked until you have followed and truly started the previous group: at least two followed collections, with at least two films watched in each (if there is only one, that one is enough). Once a group is open, it stays open even if you unfollow the collections that unlocked it.
The Atlas tab lists countries, currents, decades, genres and directors. The circle on the left shows where you stand. The stars icon in the top bar opens the sky map.

Journey gathers your rank, weekly quests and collections in progress. Rank moves slowly: it is a state of mind, not a counter. XP comes mostly from quests (Bronze 100, Silver 250, Gold 500). A film watched for the first time grants 25 XP only when it belongs to a collection you follow.
A current is a movement, style or school (New Wave, film noir, neorealism…). It links films beyond country or year. You will find them in the Atlas and in collections.

Badges reward exploration milestones (first film, number of countries, silent films…). They do not replace rank: they are path souvenirs, unlocked once and for all. They are grouped by rarity, from extra to headliner, and by code within each tier. Profile shows up to 3 chosen badges. Locked badges appear in black and white.

XP mostly measures consistency. A film watched for the first time grants 25 XP only when it belongs to a collection you are following at that moment. Weekly quests remain the large source (Bronze 100, Silver 250, Gold 500). Level follows a fixed curve and never goes down.

The small circle beside a country, current, decade or genre shows where you stand. Dotted and faint: nothing watched yet. Colored arc: you have started. Full ivory ring: broadly explored. Gold ring: everything watched. Gold ring with a center dot: you truly master that territory. Followed collections reuse the same gold: bar and titles, a check when finished, a padlock while the group is still closed.
Congratulations, you have finished the “%1$s” collection.
Congratulations! You have unlocked the “%1$s” badge!
Pinch to zoom, drag to travel, tap a star.
The film sits in the centre, with what binds it around. A farther film is less related. Tap a film to recentre, tap the rest for the fiche or the list.
Gold at the centre: chosen film. Farther = less related. Empty circle: not explored yet.

The sky map starts from a film: director, countries, genres nearby; other films farther if they share less. In the light theme the sky switches to paper so lists stay readable; each kind keeps its colour. The same name is shown only once. The Countries / Currents chips keep the territory views. A tap opens the fiche or the list. Open it from the Atlas tab, stars icon in the top bar. Pinch to zoom.
Urbinema is a path through cinema history. You mark films as watched, follow collections, and rank describes where you stand. This guide is six pages.
Home shows collections in progress, this week’s quests, and a film to pick up. It is a starting point, not a log of everything you have seen.
Countries, currents, decades, genres and directors. The circle on the left shows where you stand. The stars icon opens the sky map, around a film.

A collection is a short editorial path. You can follow ten at once. A film from a followed collection, marked watched for the first time, grants 25 XP. A long press on a film offers to mark it watched.
This tab currently gathers your rank, quests and collections in progress. A teaching page, with currents linked together, will arrive here later.
Your name, rank and badges. A tap on the rank opens the chain of ten ranks, scrolled to yours. Settings are at the top right.
The catalogue and the history notes lean on books and public lists. They are not partners: they are the landmarks used to choose and place the films.
Claude-Jean Philippe, 100 films pour une cinémathèque idéale.
Dictionnaire des films, Georges Sadoul and Émile Breton.
Dictionnaire du cinéma africain (volume 1), Éditions Karthala.
Historical Dictionary of Middle Eastern Cinema, Terri Ginsberg and Chris Lippard.
Genres et mouvements au cinéma, Vincent Pinel, Larousse.
Torgeir Holljen Thon, 100 norske filmer du må se (2008).
They Shoot Pictures, Don’t They (TSPDT), 21st edition, the 1,000 greatest films.
Letterboxd, public lists, including a copy of the TSPDT list.
Sight & Sound / BFI, 2022 once-a-decade poll (critics and directors).
Roger Ebert, Great Movies (books and the rogerebert.com archive).
Palmarès and archives of international festivals: Cannes, Venice, Berlin, FESPACO, Golden Horse, Sundance.
The Movie Database (TMDB), for the bundled posters. The app data stays on the device.
KMDb, the official database of the Korean Film Archive.
Retrospective dossiers: the British Film Institute (Sight & Sound) and CNN’s historical list of Asian cinema masterpieces.
